headline: SAFF holds at 4.32 on Female Daily (all brands flat vs 31 Oct); no new SAFF complaints, but longevity doubts on 'Extrait' scents and fake-bottle risk remain the key watch points.
kpis_note: Awareness and NPS need a consumer survey; they are not measured from public web data.

insights.text: SAFF's Female Daily rating is flat at 4.32 on 1,746 reviews, the most of any brand tracked; it trails only Alchemist (4.43). No brand or product rating moved since 31 Oct.
S.O.T.B still holds a third of SAFF's reviews at 4.1; recent reviews praise 6–8 hour wear, but one calls it heady and 'too common now'.
Packaging is the most repeated SAFF pain point: the new bottle is hard to carry (Loui) and Eulalie's bottle scores 5.9/10 on Parfumo, though Troupe reviewers like the upgraded look.
Longevity is mixed by scent: Troupe has 95% recommend, yet some reviewers get only 4–5 hours on skin and say the 'Extrait' label over-promises; Cascavel's recommend rate is lowest seen (86%).
SAFF is reaching new markets: 10 scents in 8 ml minis now sell in Japan (Don Quijote, 1,650 yen), while retailers publish guides on spotting fake SAFF bottles.

recommendations.text: Dig into S.O.T.B and Loui low-star reviews (marketplace export) to see if 'too strong / headache' is a pattern, then add wear guidance (spray count, day vs night) to product pages.
Set clear longevity expectations per scent (e.g. hours on skin vs fabric) so the 'Extrait' label does not over-promise; start with Troupe and Cascavel.
Add a travel or slim bottle and review Eulalie's bottle design; ask QC to check leaks and outer-box damage in shipping.
Publish an official 'how to spot a fake' guide (batch code, hologram, official stores) on SAFF channels and product pages, including for Japan buyers.
Run a short quarterly survey (awareness, consideration, NPS) so the report covers all brand health KPIs, not only online sentiment.
